fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Decision-load risk from simultaneous unfamiliar transfer-lane assignments at high-volume express-collector points is a genuine driver-behaviour/collision-migration hazard appropriate to a planning-stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is anchored by a verbatim EV-CA-003 quote on avoiding collisions elsewhere along the route, combined with recorded corridor facts (AADT 420,000, three-interchange permission revision concurrent with signage rationalisation); no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: CRSAG planning-stage semantics respected: the quoted audit-objective language correctly frames an off-network safety impact, and the finding remains categorically a safety concern with no compliance question conflated into it (normative_basis_note appropriately null).
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable—sequential one-interchange-per-quarter rollout with before/after speed-differential monitoring—and is operationally viable for staged corridor implementation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not applicable since a controlled-access express-collector mainline excludes pedestrians and cyclists, but the finding explicitly acknowledges this and scopes road users to vehicle occupants.

justifications.substance: An unresolved inter-agency conflict over express-collector transfer continuity genuinely threatens the Stage 1 audit scope boundary and could exclude redistributed movements across all three interchanges, a substantive planning-stage completeness issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal documentation duty is anchored by verbatim quotes EV-CA-038 (accept/conditionally accept/reject with documented reasons) and EV-CA-003 (clearly specified and consistently documented procedure), while the record conflict itself is a recorded input fact rather than invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a compliance_question distinct from any asserted safety deficiency, uses the Alberta Stage 1 equivalency (EV-CA-006) appropriately, and invokes the §5.6.2 response discipline only as a documentation standard without converting it into a safety claim.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names both conflicting records, identifies the ministry planning office as counterpart, requires documented resolution reasons under the cited discipline, and forces an explicit scope-boundary decision before finalisation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not directly applicable on a controlled-access mainline, but the finding explicitly acknowledges propagation of continuity outcomes to downstream arterials carrying pedestrians and cyclists while refraining from asserting unsupported VRU exposure.
